question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct preposition: 'The newly appointed director is responsible __ overseeing the regional operations.'

hint_ladder.title: Alamin ang Kasunod
hint_ladder.text: Ano ba ang kasunod ng blank — tao o trabaho? Basahin ulit: 'overseeing the regional operations'.

hint_ladder.title: Ang Rule ng 'Responsible'
hint_ladder.text: Alamin: 'responsible to' ay para sa boss; 'responsible for' ay para sa trabahong hawak mo.

hint_ladder.title: Gamitin ang Rule
hint_ladder.text: Dito, 'overseeing operations' ay trabaho. So aling preposition ang tama para sa trabaho?

hint_ladder.title: Final na Sagot
hint_ladder.text: Kung trabaho, 'for' ang kasama. Alin sa mga pagpipilian ang 'for'?

A.text: Correct. 'Responsible for' is the standard pairing when in charge of a task like overseeing operations.

B.text: You might have chosen B because phrases like 'charged with' sound similar, but 'responsible' pairs with 'for', not 'with'.

C.text: You might have chosen C because you know 'responsible to' is for people, but here the object is a task, not a boss.

D.text: You might have chosen D because 'involved in' misleads you, but 'responsible in' is not an English idiom.

next_time_rule: Pag may 'responsible,' tanungin: Sino o Ano? Kung tao, gamit 'to'; kung trabaho, gamit 'for'.
blueprint_id: Prepositional Idioms — Responsible For vs Responsible To
deconstruct_text:
Step 1: Identify the Anchor Element (subject, antecedent, tense marker)
Focus on 'responsible.' It pairs with 'for' or 'to' — depende kung sino o ano ang sinusundan mo, gaya ng pag-handle ng satellite office ng LGU sa probinsya.

Step 2: Recall the Corresponding Rule
Ang golden rule: 'responsible to' ay para sa tao o authority na tinatanungan mo; 'responsible for' ay para sa trabaho o tungkuling hawak mo. Think "Who vs. What."

Step 3: Eliminate Invaders and Confirm
Look at what follows: 'overseeing the regional operations' — ito ay trabaho, hindi boss. So tamang preposition ay 'for.' Option A ang tama.

**Watch-Out Zone: preposition_misuse** in action. 'Responsible to' sa task? Mali 'yan.

**Mental Trick & Rule of Thumb:**
Taglish Rule: Tanungin ang 'What?' — kapag trabaho, gamitin ang 'for' parang assignment sa barangay.
(Ask yourself: Bakit 'for' ang kailangan? Kasi tungkulin ang hawak, hindi tao.)
